result.title: Look Where Camouflage Breaks: Concealment-Guided Observation for Camouflaged Object Detection
result.summary: A camouflaged object can blend into its surroundings at one scale and become distinguishable at another. Yet a region's apparent ambiguity gives limited guidance on which observation would resolve it. The challenge is to connect the form and scale of concealment to the evidence that a new view can reveal. We introduce CamoBreak, an active framework for camouflaged object detection guided by a Concealment Spectrum. From the image and current predictions, the spectrum measures regional resemblance and boundary ambiguity across comparison scales, distinguishing persistent concealment from separation emerging at finer or broader scales. These measurements guide crop selection from the already-captured image and recognition against global foreground and background references. An object-conditioned spatial preference then selects where local evidence should update the prediction and feature memory, retaining target corrections while suppressing background distractions. Accepted corrections reshape the next measurement, while predicted segmentation benefit determines whether to observe again. Experiments across encoder families and related segmentation tasks show consistent improvements. Targeted analyses support improved small-target recovery, multiple-object coverage, and selective evidence integration. Code will be released.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 CamoBreak 主动式伪装目标检测框架，用跨尺度比较得到的「Concealment Spectrum」度量区域相似度与边界歧义，据此从已有图像中选择裁剪观察、以全局前景/背景参照做出判断，并将局部证据选择性地写入预测与特征记忆。
AI.relevance_reason: 直接对应「LOOK 与 STOP」：多尺度遮蔽度量驱动看哪里、局部证据按目标条件筛选写入状态，并以预测分割收益决定是否再观察，可供核查视觉证据筛选与停止决策的收益–成本；但方法基于单图裁剪的检测分割，不涉及 VLM 内部 latent 推理状态。
